All matches, not just the first

Source: R/par-match-all.R
par_match_all.Rd

par_match() and par_match_rows() find the first match of each element or row of x in table. These find all of them, as pairs of positions. This is a many-to-many join, such as merge() does on key columns.

  • par_match_all() compares vectors as par_match() does.

  • par_match_rows_all() compares rows as par_match_rows() does.

Usage

par_match_all(x, table, nthreads = getOption("parvenu.threads", 0L))

par_match_rows_all(x, table, nthreads = getOption("parvenu.threads", 0L))

Arguments

x

Rows to look up: a data frame, or a list of vectors of equal length.

table

Rows to look them up in, in the same form, with as many columns as x.

nthreads

A whole number: the max number of threads to use. 0 means the RAYON_NUM_THREADS environment variable, or else all cores. The default is the parvenu.threads option, or 0 if that isn't set. Inputs too small to keep that many threads busy get fewer, and more threads than cores count as all cores.

Value

A data frame with one row per pair, sorted by x and then by table. Column x is a position (or row) in x, and column table is a position in table equal to it. Elements of x with no match in table have no rows.

Details

With x and table the same, the pairs are all groups of equal elements, including each element paired with itself.

The number of pairs can be much larger than either input: 1e5 equal elements on each side make 1e10. It is counted before any pair is built. More than 2^31 - 1 pairs are an error.

The table is hashed once. As each element goes into the map, it is numbered by its group, the first equal element. Each element of x is then looked up, and the positions in table are sorted by group with a counting sort. The pairs are written on several threads. So the work beyond the hashing is linear in the number of pairs.

Examples

par_match_all(c("b", "a", "z"), c("a", "b", "a"))
#>   x table
#> 1 1     2
#> 2 2     1
#> 3 2     3

# Groups of equal rows, each pair once
keys <- data.frame(x = c(1, 2, 1, 1), y = c("a", "b", "a", "a"))
pairs <- par_match_rows_all(keys, keys)
pairs[pairs$x < pairs$table, ]
#>   x table
#> 2 1     3
#> 3 1     4
#> 7 3     4
